page: Microsoft Azure E2ps_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs using an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic operations. It is configured with 16.0 GB of memory, establishing a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local disk storage or integrated GPUs, requiring remote storage solutions such as Premium Storage for persistent filesystems.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-threaded compute efficiency alongside throughput limits associated with a dual-core footprint. The instance scores 1821.98 in stress-ng single-core execution and delivers 24.11 GB/sec during single-threaded gzip compression. Multi-threaded capacity reflects the physical core constraint, yielding a multi-core stress-ng score of 3613.78 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1987.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 21.79 GB/sec with write bandwidth measuring 13.35 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks record 1417.7 in PassMark database operations and 2.48 million operations per second during Redis SET testing.

The E2ps_v5 offers favorable resource efficiency for workloads requiring substantial memory buffers without the cost overhead of high core counts. Because compute power is limited to two physical threads, heavy concurrent processing and intensive CPU tasks will encounter resource limits. It is well suited for memory-bound services, small-scale caching layers like Redis, lightweight relational databases, and ARM-native staging or development environments.
description: Microsoft Azure E2ps_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs on an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. Built on arm64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 16.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. It features no local disk storage and no GPU hardware, relying on external network-attached storage. Benchmark testing shows balanced single-core execution, registering 1821.98 in single-core stress-ng and 24.11 GB/sec in gzip compression, while multi-core workloads are restricted by the dual-core topology. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 21.79 GB/sec, and the system achieves 2.48 million Redis SET operations per second. This hardware profile provides high memory density at low compute scale, making it suitable for lightweight databases, in-memory caches, and ARM application environments.
